# Challenger's Answer: Did Christ Have a Biological Father?

**Position.** Yes. The record names one man as the child's father, Joseph, "of the house of David." It requires the promised seed to come out of David's loins "according to the flesh." It gives "Son of God" as a covenant title, and it uses the Spirit's verbs in Luke 1:35 for empowerment and presence. I aim at the keystone D6 and at the links it stands on (D1 to D5).

---

## C1. The promised seed is out of a man's loins, according to the flesh

[L1] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"

[L2] The word for "seed" is *spermatos* (G4690, sperma, seed). It is joined to *kata sarka* (G4561, sarx, flesh), "according to the flesh."

[L3] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"

[L2] "Loins" is *osphys* (G3751): "the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power." It is the same word Hebrews uses of a father's body.

[L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."

[L3] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." [L2] "Seed" is *zera'* (H2233), seed or posterity.

[L3] Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"

[L4] The promise is sworn as seed proceeding out of David's bowels and loins (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30). Romans 1:3 says Christ was made of that seed "according to the flesh." The *osphys* of Acts 2:30 is the father's-loins word of Hebrews 7:10. So the flesh the promise names comes down a line of fathers' loins.

## C2. The tribe is reckoned by the father's house, and the named man is of David's house

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

[L3] Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls;"

[L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."

[L2] "By the house of their fathers" is *bayith* (H1004, house, family) with *'ab* (H1, father).

[L3] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L3] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."

[L4] The law declares a pedigree "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). Hebrews calls Judah's descent "evident" (Hebrews 7:14). The house Luke names at the conception is Joseph's, "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27; 2:4). So the evident descent stands on the named father's house.

**Question to the defender:** According to Hebrews 7:14, how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda," given the law, "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18)?

## C3. The father is named in four voices

- **Mary.** [L1] Luke 2:48: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- **The narrator.** [L3] Luke 2:27: "when the parents brought in the child Jesus." Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled." Luke 2:41: "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year."
- **A disciple.** [L3] John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- **The angel.** [L3] Matthew 1:21: "and thou shalt call his name JESUS. [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]" Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS." The naming is the father's act, as the angel tells Zacharias: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John" (Luke 1:13). It is also shown at Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."

[L4] The mother says "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The narrator says "his parents" (Luke 2:41). The angel gives the father's naming act to Joseph (Matthew 1:21), as he gave it to Zacharias (Luke 1:13). So the father the record names is Joseph.

## C4. The union, as the rows lay it out

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man..."

[L3] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law calls a betrothed damsel a wife.

[L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L4] Three things are footed on these rows:
1. They were husband and wife from the espousal: "her husband" (Matthew 1:19), "thy wife" (Matthew 1:20), "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
2. The canon's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1).
3. "Till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after he "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24).

So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the seed is of his loins (C1).

---

## PRESSES ON THE DEFENDER'S CHAIN

### LINK D1: "of the Holy Ghost" as the begetter

[L1] Matthew 1:20, quoted whole above: "Joseph, thou son of David ... that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

[L2] The begetting verb is *gennaō* (G1080): "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate." The *ek* in "of the Holy Ghost" has the same verb and preposition that are said of believers born "of God."

[L3] 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]"

[L3] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

[L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

[L4] The words *gennaō* and *ek* with God or the Spirit name a spiritual origin in men who had fleshly fathers (1 John 5:1; John 1:13). John 3:6 keeps flesh-birth and Spirit-birth as two kinds. Romans 1:3 adds "according to the flesh" when it means fleshly origin, and that qualifier stands at Romans 1:3. So "of the Holy Ghost" marks a covenant origin. It fits a row that names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" in the same sentence.

**The verbs of Luke 1:35.**

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."

[L2] "Come upon" is *eperchomai* (G1904). "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982).

[L3] Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me. [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]"

[L3] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."

[L3] Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. [into...: or, in every street]"

[L4] Here the same two verbs mean power given to the apostles (Acts 1:8), the cloud's presence (Luke 9:34), and healing (Acts 5:15). So in Luke 1:35 they are words of empowerment and presence on Mary.

### LINK D2: "a virgin who knew no man when she conceived"

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ou ginōskō* is present active indicative. It states her condition at the hour she spoke.

[L3] Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." The conception is future: "thou shalt conceive."

[L4] Mary's present-tense words describe the moment of the announcement, and the angel's verbs put the conception after it (Luke 1:31, 35). So Luke 1:34 dates her state before the conception and fits the espousal of C4.

**The Rebekah match.**

[L1] Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her. [very...: Heb. good of countenance]" [L2] The word behind "virgin" here is *bethulah* (H1330).

[L3] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." [L2] The word here is *'almah* (H5959).

[L3] The KJV renders *'almah* (H5959: 7 verses) as "the maid" (Exodus 2:8), "the damsels" (Psalm 68:25), "a maid" (Proverbs 30:19), and "virgins" (Song of Solomon 1:3).

[L4] The clause "neither had any man known her" stands in the *bethulah* verse (Genesis 24:16), and the *'almah* verse (Genesis 24:43) carries the noun alone. So D2's L3 carries Genesis 24:16's clause across onto a different Hebrew word.

### LINK D3: Matthew 1:16

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] *Egennēthē ex hēs* uses the passive of *gennaō*: "of the father, but by extension of the mother." The feminine *hēs* names the mother's side of the birth.

[L3] Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named at Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."

[L4] "Born of women" is said of John, whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13). Matthew draws the begat-line to "Joseph the husband of Mary" (Matthew 1:16), and the angel calls him "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). So verse 16 names the mother of the birth, inside a line that runs to the named father.

**Luke 3:23.**

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

[L2] *Nomizō* (G3543): "from νόμος; properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard:-- suppose, thing, be wont."

[L3] Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." This has the same verb form, *enomizeto*, and it is a custom, not an error.

[L4] The verb names what is held by law or usage (lexicon), as at the river-side "where prayer was wont to be made" (Acts 16:13). It stands in the same Gospel as Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48). So Luke 3:23 records the reckoning by the father's house (Numbers 1:18).

### LINK D4: Matthew 1:25

[L1] Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph ... took unto him his wife." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

[L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." [L2] *Prin ē synelthein autous* dates the finding before their coming together.

[L4] Matthew's order is:
1. the finding (1:18);
2. the taking into his house (1:24);
3. "knew her not till" the birth (1:25), with "till" (*heōs hou*) setting an end.

So the abstinence covers the pregnancy after the taking. Joseph's "he called his name JESUS" closes the same verse with the father's act (Luke 1:13).

### LINK D5: the "son of Joseph" sayings

[L1] Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." These are the words of the mother who heard the angel (Luke 1:34).

[L3] John 1:45: "We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." This is a disciple's confession.

[L4] D5 sets aside John 6:42 as the crowd's unbelief. The same title is also in the mouth of a believing disciple (John 1:45) and of Mary herself (Luke 2:48). So "son of Joseph" is the testimony of the mother and a disciple.

### LINK D6 (keystone): "Son of God for that reason"

[L1] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"

[L2] The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, and does not point forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34. The verb of v.35 is *klēthēsetai*, "shall be called."

[L3] The title stands beside a fleshly father in other rows:
- 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." David's son and God's son are named in one verse.
- 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- Psalm 2:7: "Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee. [the decree: or, for a decree]" The New Testament applies this verse:
  - at the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee";
  - at the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee";
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"
- Romans 1:4: "declared to be the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]"

[L4] "Son of God" is the covenant title God gave Solomon while David was his father (1 Chronicles 28:6). The New Testament applies its "begotten" to the resurrection and the priesthood (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 5:5), and Romans 1:3-4 sets it beside "the seed of David according to the flesh." So D6's "for that reason" assigns the title to a cause that Luke 1:32 and Romans 1:4 assign elsewhere.

**Hebrews 10:5 and Galatians 4:4.**

[L1] Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same." Hebrews 2:16: "but he took on him the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]" Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren."

[L3] Galatians 4:4, "made of a woman," is the mortality phrase:
- Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"
- Genesis 4:25: Eve calls Seth "another seed," and the verse opens "And Adam knew his wife again." [Seth: Heb. Sheth: that is Appointed, or, Put]

[L4] The prepared body was made "likewise" and "in all things ... like unto his brethren" (Hebrews 2:14, 17). Eve's "seed" had Adam as father (Genesis 4:25). So "her seed" and "made of a woman" name the mother within a body made like his brethren's.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

**1. LINK D6.** The defender wrote: "Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived of the Holy Ghost in a virgin and is called the Son of God for that reason"

- ASSUMES: the seed of David according to the flesh reaches the child through Mary.
- ROWS GIVE: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27); "because he was of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4); "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), whose house is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).
- PRESSED WITH: Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30; Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:18; Luke 1:32; 1 Chronicles 28:6.

**2. LINK D6.** The defender wrote: "Dio kai ("therefore also") makes the title "Son of God" follow from this manner of conception."

- ASSUMES: the "therefore" of Luke 1:35 points forward to a begetting of flesh.
- ROWS GIVE: "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32); "in that he hath raised up Jesus again ... this day have I begotten thee" (Acts 13:33).
- PRESSED WITH: Luke 1:32; Acts 13:33; Hebrews 5:5; Hebrews 1:5; Romans 1:4.

**3. LINK D1.** The defender wrote: "Together they give the source of the conception as the Holy Ghost, and the child "born of thee", of Mary."

- ASSUMES: *ek pneumatos hagiou* names a begetter of flesh.
- ROWS GIVE: "is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat" (1 John 5:1); "that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" (John 3:6); "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" (Acts 1:8).
- PRESSED WITH: 1 John 5:1; John 1:13; John 3:6; Acts 1:8; Luke 9:34.

**4. LINK D2.** The defender wrote: "The word the KJV renders "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is the same word it renders "virgin" for Rebekah. Her virginity is stated in Genesis 24:16 with the clause "neither had any man known her"."

- ASSUMES: the clause of Genesis 24:16 stands on the word *'almah*.
- ROWS GIVE: Genesis 24:16, "a virgin, neither had any man known her," on *bethulah* (H1330); Genesis 24:43, "when the virgin cometh forth," on *'almah* (H5959); and *'almah* as "the maid" (Exodus 2:8) and "the damsels" (Psalm 68:25).
- PRESSED WITH: Genesis 24:16; Genesis 24:43; Exodus 2:8; Psalm 68:25.

**5. LINK D2.** The defender wrote: "Mary's own words in Luke 1:34 confirm that she was a virgin who knew no man."

- ASSUMES: the present tense of Luke 1:34 describes her state at the conception.
- ROWS GIVE: "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34, present indicative); "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" (Luke 1:31, future).
- PRESSED WITH: Luke 1:31; Luke 1:35; Matthew 1:20.

**6. LINK D3.** The defender wrote: "Enomizeto (was supposed, was reckoned) marks the sonship as an opinion held by others."

- ASSUMES: *nomizō* carries a verdict of error.
- ROWS GIVE: "properly, to do by law (usage) ... be wont" (G3543); "where prayer was wont to be made" (Acts 16:13); "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48).
- PRESSED WITH: Acts 16:13; Luke 2:48; Numbers 1:18.

**7. LINK D4.** The defender wrote: "Matthew 1:25 then states that he did not know her until she gave birth."

- ASSUMES: the span of Matthew 1:25 reaches back before "took unto him his wife."
- ROWS GIVE: "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:24-25); "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19); "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24); "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1).
- PRESSED WITH: Matthew 1:24; Matthew 1:19; Deuteronomy 22:24; Genesis 4:1.

**8. LINK D5.** The defender wrote: "Scripture presents the human nature as taken from the woman, and the body as one God prepared."

- ASSUMES: "her seed" and "made of a woman" set the woman as the flesh's whole source.
- ROWS GIVE: "And Adam knew his wife again ... another seed instead of Abel" (Genesis 4:25); "Among them that are born of women ... John the Baptist" (Matthew 11:11), with "Zacharias ... thou shalt call his name John" (Luke 1:13); "he also himself likewise took part of the same" (Hebrews 2:14).
- PRESSED WITH: Genesis 4:25; Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13; Hebrews 2:14; Hebrews 2:17.

---

**Summary.** The seed is David's "according to the flesh," "of the fruit of his loins" (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30). The tribe is "evident" by "the house of their fathers" (Hebrews 7:14; Numbers 1:18). The named house is Joseph's (Luke 1:27). The mother says "thy father" (Luke 2:48). The angel joins "of the Holy Ghost" to "Joseph, thou son of David" in one verse (Matthew 1:20). On those rows, Christ's flesh came as his brethren's came, and the father is Joseph.

CHALLENGER (record's reading) -- ROUND 2, CLOSING AND PREMISE LIST

# Closing Challenge: Did Christ Have a Biological Father?

**Position.** Yes. The defender's keystone, D6, now rests on one new bridge from the link round: that "the seed of David" came "in being made of the woman." Each witness below carries its layers and answers the bridge from the text. The links are taken in order of weight.

---

## 1. LINK D6: the channel of the seed

**The defender's bridge.** It sets Romans 1:3 beside Galatians 4:4 because both use *ginomai* with *ek*.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"

[L2] The source noun is *sperma* (G4690): "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring." The verb is *ginomai* (G1096): "to become (come into being), used with great latitude." The verb is shared. The source nouns differ: *sperma* in Romans 1:3 and *gynē* in Galatians 4:4.

[L3] Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"

[L3] Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." It stands with Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."

[L4] The defender granted in the link round that "born of women" and "her seed" sit beside a named father (Luke 1:13; Genesis 4:25). "Made of a woman" belongs to the same family of phrases as Job 14:1. Romans 1:3 gives the seed-word, *sperma*, whose lexicon sense is the male seed. So the two clauses name two sources: the seed (Romans 1:3) and the mother (Galatians 4:4). Neither is a channel for the other.

**The defender's "loins at any distance."**

[L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."

[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;"

[L2] *Osphys* (G3751): "internally (by extension) procreative power."

[L4] Levi was in Abraham's loins across generations, and Matthew 1:2 shows the path: father begat son, three times. A remote loins-descent is a chain of begetting fathers. Acts 2:30's "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" therefore runs down such a chain. The chain the Gospels draw ends at "Joseph the husband of Mary" (Matthew 1:16), "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). It fits my first link.

**The defender's answer on Hebrews 7:14.** The defender said the descent is "evident" because the pedigree is published.

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

[L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."

[L2] "Declared their pedigrees" is *yalad* (H3205): "to bear young; causatively, to beget; ... specifically, to show lineage; ... declare pedigrees." The registry verb is the begetting verb.

[L3] Ezra 2:61-62: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name: ... therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood. [were they...: Heb. they were polluted from the priesthood]"

[L4] The law's pedigree is declared with the begetting verb, by the fathers' house (Numbers 1:18). Ezra 2:61-62 puts out a house reckoned by the wife's name. The defender routes the flesh through Mary, and the house the rows give her is a kinship with "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5). Hebrews 7:14's "evident ... out of Juda" fits the named father's house: Joseph, "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27).

## 2. LINK D6: the title

**The defender's own division of Romans 1:3-4.** It places the Davidic seed under "flesh" and the title under "the spirit of holiness."

[L1] Romans 1:4: "And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]"

[L2] *Horizō* (G3724): "to mark out or bound ... appoint, decree."

[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father."

[L4] By the defender's own division, the flesh belongs to "the seed of David" and the title to the spirit, appointed "by the resurrection." That is the Solomon pattern: David's son in the flesh, and God's son by appointment, in one verse. So the title stands apart from any begetting of the flesh.

**The defender's *dio kai*.**

[L1] Luke 1:32: "and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

[L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] Both verses carry *kaleō* (G2564), "to call," in "shall be called." The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, and does not point forward to biological divine paternity.

[L4] Verse 32 gives the title together with the throne of David. Verse 35 restates the same calling. The result clause of v.35 is a calling, and the conception verb stands in v.31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**The defender's John 3:16.**
